conflicts.point: Whether private clean energy additionality and behind-the-meter generation contracts effectively isolate regional power grids from high-density computing demand surges.

positions.stance: Private clean energy contracts and dedicated microgrids bypass public grid congestion and prevent local ratepayer cost-shifting.
Private power purchase agreements draw from shared regional transmission networks and shift transmission upgrade costs onto residential ratepayers.

conflicts.point: Whether the Federal Trade Commission possesses the statutory authority under Section 5 of the FTC Act to impose utility-style structural separation and mandatory ratepayer protections on dominant compute clusters.

positions.stance: Section 5 of the FTC Act provides statutory authority to enforce structural splits and rate rules comparable to the 1982 AT&T divestiture.
Applying antitrust enforcement to restrict physical data center development creates harmful bureaucratic friction that outweighs potential market corrections.

conflicts.point: Whether hardware-level telemetry and pre-deployment safety gates effectively govern frontier capabilities or merely impose compliance barriers that protect large incumbents.

positions.stance: Mandatory hardware telemetry and ASML semiconductor tracking provide necessary chokepoints to prevent unmanaged capability surges.
Silicon-level tracking cannot inspect encrypted API reasoning traces and disproportionately burdens smaller market entrants.

verdicts.conflict: Whether private clean energy additionality and behind-the-meter generation contracts effectively isolate regional power grids from high-density computing demand surges.
verdicts.rationale: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission data showing five-year interconnection delays and rising capacity prices gives the skeptic position stronger empirical grounding. The accelerationist view relies on theoretical isolation that ignores shared transmission infrastructure realities.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical data demonstrating that dedicated microgrids operate entirely off-grid without drawing from shared transmission lines or raising local capacity prices.

verdicts.conflict: Whether the Federal Trade Commission possesses the statutory authority under Section 5 of the FTC Act to impose utility-style structural separation and mandatory ratepayer protections on dominant compute clusters.
verdicts.rationale: Both positions lack sufficient legal precedent and implementation detail regarding how antitrust statutes apply to physical data center assets. Deciding this requires clearer judicial interpretation of Section 5 authority over modern physical and digital infrastructure bottlenecks.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: A federal court ruling testing the limits of Section 5 authority against physical compute infrastructure investments.

verdicts.conflict: Whether hardware-level telemetry and pre-deployment safety gates effectively govern frontier capabilities or merely impose compliance barriers that protect large incumbents.
verdicts.rationale: The accelerationist critique correctly identifies a logical enforcement gap where hardware tracking cannot inspect encrypted API reasoning traces. This makes broad silicon tracking both burdensome for new entrants and ineffective for safety verification.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Proven cryptographic auditing methods that verify model capabilities at the silicon level without decrypting proprietary reasoning traces.
